newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down on Thursday on overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
The most actively traded August 1997 contract ended at 22,900 yuan ($2,761) per tonne, losing 140 yuan.
It opened at 22,880 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 22,800 and a high of 22,940 yuan per tonne.
May ended unchanged at 23,200, June fell 50 to 23,100, July lost 90 to 22,930 and September shed 70 to 22,930 yuan.
Combined volume fell to 31,600 tonnes from 39,860 tonnes.
Copper opened lower and fell further for most of the session before speculative buying set in to push prices from their lows.
Traders said sentiment was steady despite the day's falls.
"LME losses were the major factor today but there was no sign of panic, and that helped prices emerge from the lows at the close," one trader said.
"Many investors do not believe copper futures can fall sharply on the current market fundamentals," he said.
Traders said strong physical spot prices would balance a generally pessimistic outlook for copper futures. Physical prices are around 23,300 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area.
"Physical and futures prices will slide slowly in the long run -- at least that's what the fundamentals show. But I don't see any good chance of sharp falls," a second trader said.
Traders said they expected copper to move around the 23,000 yuan level in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down. May did not trade. June fell 200 to 15,600 and July lost 100 to 15,800 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 160 tonnes from 250 tonnes.
